qualitative.source: claude-code subagent (viewed all 5 contact sheets + profile + transcript)
qualitative.summary: A 36-minute chaptered country portrait of Kazakhstan moving from nomadic tradition (eagle hunters, yurt raising, steppe games) through natural wonders (Kaindy's sunken forest, Mangystau's striped badlands, fossil hunting) to a state-guided tour of Astana's AI and tech institutions, and finally a long, atmospheric exploration of the Baikonur Cosmodrome and its abandoned Buran shuttle hangar. It is the most music-led opening of the six: 20 s of pure landscape before the single word 'Mars', then 'Welcome to Kazakhstan'. Throughout, Joe is accompanied by a local creator-guide and hosted by officials; welcome performances and costumed hosts recur. Visual devices include an illustrated map, Soviet archival film with an AP bug, red 'TOP!' sticker graphics and date captions. It ends on a gift-giving goodbye, then a wordless reprise of the landscapes from the opening (badlands, yurt on green hills) with no sponsor read.
qualitative.hook_analysis: Visual/musical cold open: green steppe (0:00), a lone rider in badlands (0:10), pink-lit mesas (0:20), first word 'Mars' at 0:20, costumed welcome (0:30), peaks above cloud (0:40). A second sizzle (0:44-1:21) adds a horse beside a lying man, then a space-heritage tease - rocket hall (1:29-1:49) and a retro TV showing a launch (1:59) - with VO 'humanity took its very first step beyond Earth', foreshadowing the Baikonur finale. Replay peak 0:00-0:21; overall peak 10:48 in the context section.
qualitative.narrative_arc: 7 chapters: Welcome (0:00-2:03) -> Eagle tradition, Almaty (2:03-5:42) -> Nomadic tents, yurt building and steppe games (5:42-9:02) -> Modernizing Kazakhstan: Kaindy lake, cable car, exposition on economy with archival and officials (9:02-11:08) -> Geological wonders: Caspian boat, Mangystau badlands, fossils (11:08-14:24) -> Astana and tech: airport welcome, music hall, alem.ai centre, government briefings, mosque (14:24-22:59) -> Baikonur: archival history, launch pad, evacuation tunnel, Buran hangar (22:59-35:22) -> wordless landscape coda (35:32-36:02).
qualitative.camera_and_composition: Extreme-wide drone/long-lens landscapes with tiny figures (0:10, 8:36, 12:34, 13:23 figure on a cliff against the moon). Detail inserts of eagle talons (2:59, 3:58-4:08) and fossil teeth in palms (13:43-13:53). Symmetrical overhead looks down rocket gantries and hangar wells (32:54-33:43). Corridor depth shots in the bunker tunnel (28:26-29:05). Joe frequently framed in profile beside a guide in a 50/50 two-shot. Camera moves not observable at storyboard resolution.
qualitative.color_and_grade: Saturated cool grade with teal shadows: lush greens on the steppe, cyan water at Kaindy (9:15-9:35), pastel pink/white striped badlands (12:34, 35:32). Astana tech interiors push purple/blue neon (18:11-19:10). Baikonur is cyan-teal and industrial; archival Soviet film (23:08-23:58) is warm and faded, a deliberate contrast.
qualitative.sound_and_music: Speech coverage ~50%; longest non-speech stretch ~81 s (the 13:03-14:24 badlands montage). Speech-free montages recur at chapter ends (8:40-9:02, 13:03-14:24, 21:43-21:59), consistent with music-carried transitions. Diegetic music at Almaty folk ensemble (2:29) and jaw-harp/dombra performers in Astana (14:53-16:22). No sponsor read; closes with a like/subscribe line.
what_to_borrow: Open with 20 s of pure landscape and a one-word line before the thesis
Plant the finale in the opening (rocket hall and TV launch at 1:29-1:59 pay off at Baikonur)
End a chapter on a long wordless landscape montage to reset the viewer
Use overhead symmetry and long corridors to make abandoned industrial space feel monumental
Close with a wordless reprise of the opening's best landscapes
what_to_avoid_copying: The long government/tech-institution segment (16:32-21:19) reads as hosted promotion and stalls the pace
Archival clips carrying a third-party AP bug (23:48)
Cartoon 'TOP!' sticker graphics (31:04, 31:54) clash with the cinematic Buran sequence

observations.name: detail inserts as cutaways

observations.name: natural wonder reveal
observations.description: Aerial of Kaindy lake (9:05), drowned trees (9:15), underwater trunks (9:35), cable car (9:45).

observations.name: exposition with archival and officials
observations.description: Soviet-era assembly footage (10:05), oil pump (10:25), handshake with a minister with subtitle (10:45); replay peak 10:48.

observations.name: longest wordless landscape montage
observations.description: Mangystau striped badlands from above and a figure on a cliff against the moon (12:34-14:13).

observations.name: subtitled expert + hand insert
observations.description: Fossil teeth in a guide's palm (13:43-13:53) and guide on a ridge with English subtitles (14:03).

observations.name: institutional tech tour
observations.description: alem.ai centre, neon exhibits, government briefings with on-screen slides (16:42-21:19).

observations.name: illustrated map + archival history
observations.description: Hand-illustrated Kazakhstan map (22:49-22:59) then warm Soviet archival film of Baikonur (23:08-23:58), one clip with an AP bug.

observations.name: tunnel tension beat
observations.description: Narrow bunker corridors and a black frame (28:26-29:05) under 'it's not ending'; replay peak 28:50.

observations.name: abandoned-hangar set-piece
observations.description: Buran shuttle and Energia rocket in a decaying hangar shot from overhead and low angles (30:35-34:23), with 'NOVEMBER 15, 1988' date card (31:44).

observations.name: gift goodbye + wordless reprise
observations.description: Group with gifted rocket model (35:12), night two-shot (35:22), then badlands and a lone yurt on green hills (35:32-35:52) echoing the opening.

limitations: Frames are YouTube storyboard previews (YouTube storyboard 320x180, one frame every 9.9s). Camera moves are measured only when consecutive samples fall in the same shot (slow, sustained moves); transitions only when a sample lands inside one (counts are lower bounds); individual cut points are not observable.
Shot types use face/sky/edge heuristics on low-resolution frames - treat as approximate.
